Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

## To do
* [x] change to one `can_has` function per backend. Pass in function name, it can still distribute the work if it wants to.
* [x] function naming, should it be `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error` or `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error`? The latter seems nicer, but I don't know how to do it
* [ ] documentation for users
* [ ] documentation for backend authors
* [ ] discuss: what other information to store in the `BackendInformation` object? 
	* homepage URL
	* fancy name? (different from the name used in the entry point)
	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

## To do
* [x] change to one `can_has` function per backend. Pass in function name, it can still distribute the work if it wants to.
* [x] function naming, should it be `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error` or `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error`? The latter seems nicer, but I don't know how to do it
* [ ] documentation for users
* [ ] documentation for backend authors
* [ ] discuss: what other information to store in the `BackendInformation` object? 
	* homepage URL
	* fancy name? (different from the name used in the entry point)
	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

Embarrassingly parallel algorithms

Embarrassingly parallel algorithms are those that can be easily and efficiently divided into smaller, independent tasks that can be executed concurrently across multiple processing units, such as CPUs, GPUs, or nodes, without requiring significant communication or synchronisation between them. This type of parallelism is often referred to as “embarrassingly parallel” because it’s so straightforward and easy to implement. Refer [this](https://joblib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/parallel.html) to see how to implement embarrassingly parallel algorithms using joblib.

Characteristics of Embarrassingly Parallel Problems(Algorithms):

- Independent tasks: Each task can be executed independently, without relying on the output of other tasks.
- No communication: Tasks do not require frequent or significant communication with each other.
- No data dependencies: Tasks do not rely on shared data or intermediate results from other tasks.
- Easy to divide: The problem can be easily split into smaller, parallelizable tasks.

## Adding a new algorithm to nx-parallel

### Step 1 : Find a NetworkX algorithm that is embarrassingly parallel

- You can find such an algorithm from the NetworkX's references - https://networkx.org/documentation/latest/reference/index.html
- Make sure there is a `_dispatchable` decorator(in the networkx's codebase) on the algorithm you have selected to parallelise.

### Step 2 : Complete the checklist in Contributor's guide

This [checklist](https://github.com/networkx/nx-parallel/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#general-guidelines-on-adding-a-new-algorithm) in Contributor's guide for adding a new algorithm to the package.

## Some references:

It would be better to look at [currently existing algorithms](https://github.com/networkx/nx-parallel/tree/main/nx_parallel/algorithms) than previous PRs that add parallel algorithms(like https://github.com/networkx/nx-parallel/pull/60 , https://github.com/networkx/nx-parallel/pull/37 , https://github.com/networkx/nx-parallel/pull/45 and many more) because we have changed a few things. 



Feel free to ask questions if you get stuck anywhere or if anything is not clear or if you want something to be explained in a bit more detail here.

+Dispatching
+===========
+
+The dispatching mechanism allows users to use alternative implementations of the algorithms
+available in scikit-image. The alternative implementations are provided by separate
+Python packages maintained outside of scikit-image. Example use-cases are support for array
+libraries other than Numpy or optimised implementations for particular hardware.
+
+This section of the documentation describes how to create an alternative implementation (a "backend")
+and how the dispatching mechanism in scikit-image works.
+
+.. important::
+    Dispatching support and infrastructure is experimental and is not ready for production.
+    It's made available as an early draft so that developers can gain experience
+    with the system.
+
+    Expect the dispatching API to change without notice.
+
+
+Implementing a new backend
+--------------------------
+
+An alternative implementation ("backend") is a good place to provide optimized implementations
+for particular hardware, support array libraries other than Numpy or explore novel ideas that
+are not (yet) a good fit for the core scikit-image library.
+
+To create a backend you have to create a new Python package that registers two particular
+`entrypoints <https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/pyproject-toml/#entry-points>`_. The first entrypoint called `skimage_backends` should resolve to a namespace
+that contains two functions: `can_has(name, *args, **kwargs)` and `get_implementation(name)`.
+The second entrypoint called `skimage_backend_infos` should resolve to a function with no
+arguments that returns an instance of the `skimage.util._backends.BackendInformation` class
+or something that behaves like it.
+
+
+The `skimage_backend_infos` entrypoint
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+The information your backend provides via this entrypoint is used to get things like its
+name, homepage and which functions it implements. The main requirement for this entrypoint

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

## To do
* [x] change to one `can_has` function per backend. Pass in function name, it can still distribute the work if it wants to.
* [x] function naming, should it be `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error` or `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error`? The latter seems nicer, but I don't know how to do it
* [ ] documentation for users
* [ ] documentation for backend authors
* [ ] discuss: what other information to store in the `BackendInformation` object? 
	* homepage URL
	* fancy name? (different from the name used in the entry point)
	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

+Dispatching
+===========
+
+The dispatching mechanism allows users to use alternative implementations of the algorithms
+available in scikit-image. The alternative implementations are provided by separate
+Python packages maintained outside of scikit-image. Example use-cases are support for array
+libraries other than Numpy or optimised implementations for particular hardware.
+
+This section of the documentation describes how to create an alternative implementation (a "backend")
+and how the dispatching mechanism in scikit-image works.
+
+.. important::
+    Dispatching support and infrastructure is experimental and is not ready for production.
+    It's made available as an early draft so that developers can gain experience
+    with the system.
+
+    Expect the dispatching API to change without notice.
+
+
+Implementing a new backend
+--------------------------
+
+An alternative implementation ("backend") is a good place to provide optimized implementations
+for particular hardware, support array libraries other than Numpy or explore novel ideas that
+are not (yet) a good fit for the core scikit-image library.
+
+To create a backend you have to create a new Python package that registers two particular
+`entrypoints <https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/pyproject-toml/#entry-points>`_. The first entrypoint called `skimage_backends` should resolve to a namespace
+that contains two functions: `can_has(name, *args, **kwargs)` and `get_implementation(name)`.
+The second entrypoint called `skimage_backend_infos` should resolve to a function with no
+arguments that returns an instance of the `skimage.util._backends.BackendInformation` class
+or something that behaves like it.
+
+
+The `skimage_backend_infos` entrypoint
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+The information your backend provides via this entrypoint is used to get things like its
+name, homepage and which functions it implements. The main requirement for this entrypoint
+is that it is fast to import and has no dependencies other than `scikit-image`.
+
+The return value of the function should be an instance of the
+`skimage.util._backends.BackendInformation` class or something that behaves like it.
+
+The reason this entrypoint has to be fast is that the list of implemented functions which
+it provides is used to make a decision on which scikit-image functions need decorating
+with dispatching logic.
+
+To help make your implementation fast avoid computing the list of implemented functions
+dynamically or performing other expensive operations.
+
+
+The `skimage_backends` entrypoint
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+This entrypoint should point to a namespace that contains two functions:
+`can_has(name, *args, **kwargs)` and `get_implementation(name)`. They will be used to
+determine if the backend will be called and to get the actual implementation.
+
+When a user calls a function that the backend listed as one that it implements (via
+the information endpoint) the
+`can_has` function will be called with the name of the function that is being dispatched
+and the arguments the user provided when calling the function. The `can_has` function
+should use this information to determine if the backend wants to be called or if a
+different backend should be tried. A backend might implement a particular function but
+only want to handle calls where the input arrays are of a particuler type or size.

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

## To do
* [x] change to one `can_has` function per backend. Pass in function name, it can still distribute the work if it wants to.
* [x] function naming, should it be `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error` or `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error`? The latter seems nicer, but I don't know how to do it
* [ ] documentation for users
* [ ] documentation for backend authors
* [ ] discuss: what other information to store in the `BackendInformation` object? 
	* homepage URL
	* fancy name? (different from the name used in the entry point)
	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

## To do
* [x] change to one `can_has` function per backend. Pass in function name, it can still distribute the work if it wants to.
* [x] function naming, should it be `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error` or `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error`? The latter seems nicer, but I don't know how to do it
* [ ] documentation for users
* [ ] documentation for backend authors
* [ ] discuss: what other information to store in the `BackendInformation` object? 
	* homepage URL
	* fancy name? (different from the name used in the entry point)
	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

+Dispatching
+===========
+
+The dispatching mechanism allows users to use alternative implementations of the algorithms
+available in scikit-image. The alternative implementations are provided by separate
+Python packages maintained outside of scikit-image. Example use-cases are support for array
+libraries other than Numpy or optimised implementations for particular hardware.
+
+This section of the documentation describes how to create an alternative implementation (a "backend")
+and how the dispatching mechanism in scikit-image works.
+
+.. important::
+    Dispatching support and infrastructure is experimental and is not ready for production.
+    It's made available as an early draft so that developers can gain experience
+    with the system.
+
+    Expect the dispatching API to change without notice.
+
+
+Implementing a new backend
+--------------------------
+
+An alternative implementation ("backend") is a good place to provide optimized implementations
+for particular hardware, support array libraries other than Numpy or explore novel ideas that
+are not (yet) a good fit for the core scikit-image library.
+
+To create a backend you have to create a new Python package that registers two particular
+`entrypoints <https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/pyproject-toml/#entry-points>`_. The first entrypoint called `skimage_backends` should resolve to a namespace
+that contains two functions: `can_has(name, *args, **kwargs)` and `get_implementation(name)`.
+The second entrypoint called `skimage_backend_infos` should resolve to a function with no
+arguments that returns an instance of the `skimage.util._backends.BackendInformation` class

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

* [ ] documentation for users
* [ ] documentation for backend authors
* [ ] discuss: what other information to store in the `BackendInformation` object? 
	* homepage URL
	* fancy name? (different from the name used in the entry point)
	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

## To do
* [x] change to one `can_has` function per backend. Pass in function name, it can still distribute the work if it wants to.
* [x] function naming, should it be `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error` or `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error`? The latter seems nicer, but I don't know how to do it
* [ ] documentation for users
* [ ] documentation for backend authors
* [ ] discuss: what other information to store in the `BackendInformation` object? 
	* homepage URL
	* fancy name? (different from the name used in the entry point)
	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

+def _entry_points(group):

+    all_entry_points = entry_points()

+        selected_entry_points = all_entry_points.select(group=group)
+    else:
+        selected_entry_points = all_entry_points.get(group, ())
+    return selected_entry_points

+def dispatching_disabled():

+    if no_dispatching == "1":
+        return True
+    else:
+        return False

+
+    return public_name

I am not sure if having a context manager would be useful to the scikit-image users or not. We can instead have an environment variable that stores the backend's name and I think that might be better way here because then the users wouldn't have to change their skimage code alot or write it all in a context manager. 

In NetworkX we have the `NETWORKX_BACKEND_PRIORITY` env variable. It can be either just one backend_name or a list of backend_names. And in networkx you can also dispatch using a context manager but the context manager there was introduced because we wanted to offer backend configurations. But, I'm not sure if that's something that would be very useful in the scikit-image and its backends ecosystem. (ref- https://networkx.org/documentation/latest/reference/backends.html).

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

* [x] change to one `can_has` function per backend. Pass in function name, it can still distribute the work if it wants to.
* [x] function naming, should it be `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error` or `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error`? The latter seems nicer, but I don't know how to do it
* [ ] documentation for users
* [ ] documentation for backend authors
* [ ] discuss: what other information to store in the `BackendInformation` object? 
	* homepage URL
	* fancy name? (different from the name used in the entry point)
	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

## To do
* [x] change to one `can_has` function per backend. Pass in function name, it can still distribute the work if it wants to.
* [x] function naming, should it be `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error` or `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error`? The latter seems nicer, but I don't know how to do it
* [ ] documentation for users
* [ ] documentation for backend authors
* [ ] discuss: what other information to store in the `BackendInformation` object? 
	* homepage URL
	* fancy name? (different from the name used in the entry point)
	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

## To do
* [x] change to one `can_has` function per backend. Pass in function name, it can still distribute the work if it wants to.
* [x] function naming, should it be `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error` or `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error`? The latter seems nicer, but I don't know how to do it
* [ ] documentation for users
* [ ] documentation for backend authors
* [ ] discuss: what other information to store in the `BackendInformation` object? 
	* homepage URL
	* fancy name? (different from the name used in the entry point)
	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

## To do
* [x] change to one `can_has` function per backend. Pass in function name, it can still distribute the work if it wants to.
* [x] function naming, should it be `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error` or `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error`? The latter seems nicer, but I don't know how to do it
* [ ] documentation for users
* [ ] documentation for backend authors
* [ ] discuss: what other information to store in the `BackendInformation` object? 
	* homepage URL
	* fancy name? (different from the name used in the entry point)
	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

	* homepage URL

	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

> What would be a good way to separate it into modules?

I think separating out all the helper functions/functionalities from the `_diapatchable` class might be a good start. Also, I'm not sure if separating methods(like how they are currently) of the `_dispatchable` class into different modules would make it less or more readable. For example, the refactor in PR https://github.com/networkx/networkx/pull/7761 could be said to increase the readability because there is one less indentation, but it can also be seen as adding an additional depth to the logic. Also I think for new-contributors having an extra indentation might be easier to read than to go down a level deeper into the rabbit hole. Release notes

v5.0.0

v5 Release

v5 of the Codecov GitHub Action will use the Codecov Wrapper to encapsulate the CLI. This will help ensure that the Action gets updates quicker.

Migration Guide

The v5 release also coincides with the opt-out feature for tokens for public repositories. In the Global Upload Token section of the settings page of an organization in codecov.io, you can set the ability for Codecov to receive a coverage reports from any source. This will allow contributors or other members of a repository to upload without needing access to the Codecov token. For more details see how to upload without a token.

[!WARNING]
The following arguments have been changed

  • file (this has been deprecated in favor of files)
  • plugin (this has been deprecated in favor of plugins)

The following arguments have been added:

  • binary
  • gcov_args
  • gcov_executable
  • gcov_ignore
  • gcov_include
  • report_type
  • skip_validation
  • swift_project

You can see their usage in the action.yml file.

#7724: `MultiGraph` views return inconsistent `has_edge` results.

___

Minimum working example:

```python
import networkx as nx

G = nx.MultiDiGraph()

G.add_edges_from([("a", "b"),
                  ("a", "c"),       # <-- to be filtered out
                  ("c", "b")])

H = nx.edge_subgraph(G, [("a", "b", 0), ("c", "b", 0)])

print(f"{H.edges()}\n\n"
      f"{H.has_edge('a', 'c')} \t H.has_edge('a', 'c')\n"
      f"{('a', 'c') in H.edges()} \t ('a', 'c') in H.edges()\n\n"
      f"{'c' in H['a']} \t 'c' in H['a']\n"
      f"{'c' in list(H['a'])} \t 'c' in list(H['a'])")
```

Output **before** the PR:

```
# [('a', 'b'), ('b', 'c')]
#
# True      H.has_edge('a', 'c')    # <-- inconsistent result
# False     ('a', 'c') in H.edges()
#
# True      'c' in H['a']           # <-- inconsistent result
# False     'c' in list(H['a'])
```

Output **after** the PR:

```
# [('a', 'b'), ('b', 'c')]

# False      H.has_edge('a', 'c')
# False      ('a', 'c') in H.edges()

# False      'c' in H['a']
# False      'c' in list(H['a'])

___

Minimum working example:

```python
import networkx as nx

G = nx.MultiDiGraph()

G.add_edges_from([("a", "b"),
                  ("a", "c"),       # <-- to be filtered out
                  ("c", "b")])

H = nx.edge_subgraph(G, [("a", "b", 0), ("c", "b", 0)])

print(f"{H.edges()}\n\n"
      f"{H.has_edge('a', 'c')} \t H.has_edge('a', 'c')\n"
      f"{('a', 'c') in H.edges()} \t ('a', 'c') in H.edges()\n\n"
      f"{'c' in H['a']} \t 'c' in H['a']\n"
      f"{'c' in list(H['a'])} \t 'c' in list(H['a'])")
```

Output **before** the PR:

```
# [('a', 'b'), ('b', 'c')]
#
# True      H.has_edge('a', 'c')    # <-- inconsistent result
# False     ('a', 'c') in H.edges()
#
# True      'c' in H['a']           # <-- inconsistent result
# False     'c' in list(H['a'])
```

Output **after** the PR:

```
# [('a', 'b'), ('b', 'c')]

# False      H.has_edge('a', 'c')
# False      ('a', 'c') in H.edges()

# False      'c' in H['a']
# False      'c' in list(H['a'])

Summary:

This PR introduces a new **`execute_parallel`** function that simplifies algorithm parallelization logic by obviating the need for separate joblib calls for each algorithm while enabling much greater flexibility (for developers and the user).

## Key Updates:

1. **Add `execute_parallel`**:
   - Centralizes logic for parallel execution across data chunks.
   - Uses `iterator_func` to customize how data (nodes, edges, etc.) is iterated over.
   - Supports both default and custom chunking via `get_chunks`.

2. **Remove `create_iterables`**:
   - Simplified by moving to `iterator_func` within `execute_parallel`.

3. **Thread-safe Joblib config**:
   - Added a `parallel_config` context manager that uses thread-local storage to manage Joblib settings (like backend/verbose) without interference during concurrent runs.

4. **Refactor `betweenness_centrality` & `edge_betweenness_centrality`** to use `execute_parallel` as a POC.

## Why This Matters:

- **Parsimony**: Reduces code complexity by consolidating parallel execution logic into one function, making the codebase cleaner and easier to maintain.
- **Flexibility**: `execute_parallel` and `iterator_func` make this adaptable for any graph algs that need parallelism.
- **Efficiency**: Centralized parallel logic reduces duplication.
- **Maintainability**: Easier to extend and manage without `create_iterables`.

## TODO:
- Add unit test for `execute_parallel` once the interface gets the green-light
- Perform regression test to ensure equivalent functionality
- Finish refactoring the other algorithms to incorporate `execute_parallel` in place of existing separate joblib Summary:

This PR introduces a new **`execute_parallel`** function that simplifies algorithm parallelization logic by obviating the need for separate joblib calls for each algorithm while enabling much greater flexibility (for developers and the user).

## Key Updates:

1. **Add `execute_parallel`**:
   - Centralizes logic for parallel execution across data chunks.
   - Uses `iterator_func` to customize how data (nodes, edges, etc.) is iterated over.
   - Supports both default and custom chunking via `get_chunks`.

2. **Remove `create_iterables`**:
   - Simplified by moving to `iterator_func` within `execute_parallel`.

3. **Thread-safe Joblib config**:
   - Added a `parallel_config` context manager that uses thread-local storage to manage Joblib settings (like backend/verbose) without interference during concurrent runs.

4. **Refactor `betweenness_centrality` & `edge_betweenness_centrality`** to use `execute_parallel` as a POC.

## Why This Matters:

- **Parsimony**: Reduces code complexity by consolidating parallel execution logic into one function, making the codebase cleaner and easier to maintain.
- **Flexibility**: `execute_parallel` and `iterator_func` make this adaptable for any graph algs that need parallelism.
- **Efficiency**: Centralized parallel logic reduces duplication.
- **Maintainability**: Easier to extend and manage without `create_iterables`.

- Perform regression test to ensure equivalent functionality

+
+The following backends are known to work with the current stable release of
+NetworkX.
+
+Backends need not be listed here in order to work, and there may be many
+backends that NetworkX developers don't know about. You should be able to
+install the backend, enable the backend using the `backend=...` keyword arg,
+the `NETWORKX_BACKEND_PRIORITY` environment variable, or the config setting
+`nx.config.backend_priority="..."` as described in the
+[Tutorial](/tutorial.md#using-networkx-backends).
+
+See the documentation for a particular backend for a description of
+the NetworkX functions it provides, how to install it, and any special
+backend-specific configurations it supports.
+
+```{list-table}
+:header-rows: 1
+*  - Name
+   - Description
+*  - [nx-parallel](https://github.com/networkx/nx-parallel)
+   - Parallelized implementations of various NetworkX functions using joblib
+*  - [nx-cugraph](https://rapids.ai/nx-cugraph)
+   - GPU acceleration using RAPIDS cuGraph and NVIDIA GPUs

[networkx/utils/backends.py line 2313](https://github.com/networkx/networkx/blob/c107d25c853fbfe082c12d9e8c77afe4f34e91da/networkx/utils/backends.py#L2313C9-L2313C60) causes an `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'rstrip'` when running python with the flag [`-OO`](https://docs.python.org/3/using/cmdline.html#cmdoption-OO).
### Current Behavior

`return f"{self._orig_doc.rstrip()}\n\n    {to_add}"` raises an AttributeError.
```shell
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/workspaces/bug.py", line 1, in <module>
    from networkx.utils.backends import _dispatchable
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/__init__.py", line 22, in <module>
    from networkx import classes
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/classes/__init__.py", line 6, in <module>
    from .function import *
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/classes/function.py", line 1044, in <module>
    def is_negatively_weighted(G, edge=None, weight="weight"):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/utils/backends.py", line 567, in __new__
    self = argmap(_do_nothing)(self)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/utils/decorators.py", line 793, in __call__
    func.__doc__ = f.__doc__
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/utils/backends.py", line 579, in __doc__
    rv = self._cached_doc = self._make_doc()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/utils/backends.py", line 1520, in _make_doc
    return f"{self._orig_doc.rstrip()}\n\n    {to_add}"
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'rstrip'
```

### Expected Behavior

Ignore `func.__doc__` when it is None, or set `self._orig_doc` to an empty string.

Alternatively:
Just add a disclaimer to not run with -OO flag when using networkx.

### Steps to Reproduce

bug.py
```python
from networkx.utils.backends import _dispatchable
```
Run with `python -OO bug.py`

### Environment

<!--- Please provide details about your local environment -->

Python version: 3.10
NetworkX version: 3.3

### Additional context
I am not familiar with networkx. This came up when using pytorch.compile and trying out the -OO flag, which I had never heard of. ### Current Behavior

`return f"{self._orig_doc.rstrip()}\n\n    {to_add}"` raises an AttributeError.
```shell
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/workspaces/bug.py", line 1, in <module>

  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/__init__.py", line 22, in <module>
    from networkx import classes
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/classes/__init__.py", line 6, in <module>
    from .function import *
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/classes/function.py", line 1044, in <module>
    def is_negatively_weighted(G, edge=None, weight="weight"):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/utils/backends.py", line 567, in __new__
    self = argmap(_do_nothing)(self)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/utils/decorators.py", line 793, in __call__
    func.__doc__ = f.__doc__
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/utils/backends.py", line 579, in __doc__
    rv = self._cached_doc = self._make_doc()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/utils/backends.py", line 1520, in _make_doc
    return f"{self._orig_doc.rstrip()}\n\n    {to_add}"
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'rstrip'
```

### Expected Behavior

Ignore `func.__doc__` when it is None, or set `self._orig_doc` to an empty string.

Alternatively:
Just add a disclaimer to not run with -OO flag when using networkx.

### Steps to Reproduce

bug.py
```python
from networkx.utils.backends import _dispatchable
```
Run with `python -OO bug.py`

### Environment

<!--- Please provide details about your local environment -->

Python version: 3.10
NetworkX version: 3.3

### Additional context
I am not familiar with networkx. This came up when using pytorch.compile and trying out the -OO flag, which I had never heard of. I am not sure how widespread the use of the flag is or how important it is to support it. Just seems like something to be aware of. In any case, at least this edge case will now be documented for future reference.

[networkx/utils/backends.py line 2313](https://github.com/networkx/networkx/blob/c107d25c853fbfe082c12d9e8c77afe4f34e91da/networkx/utils/backends.py#L2313C9-L2313C60) causes an `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'rstrip'` when running python with the flag [`-OO`](https://docs.python.org/3/using/cmdline.html#cmdoption-OO).
### Current Behavior

`return f"{self._orig_doc.rstrip()}\n\n    {to_add}"` raises an AttributeError.
```shell
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/workspaces/bug.py", line 1, in <module>
    from networkx.utils.backends import _dispatchable
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/__init__.py", line 22, in <module>
    from networkx import classes
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/classes/__init__.py", line 6, in <module>
    from .function import *
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/classes/function.py", line 1044, in <module>
    def is_negatively_weighted(G, edge=None, weight="weight"):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/utils/backends.py", line 567, in __new__
    self = argmap(_do_nothing)(self)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/utils/decorators.py", line 793, in __call__
    func.__doc__ = f.__doc__
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/utils/backends.py", line 579, in __doc__
    rv = self._cached_doc = self._make_doc()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/networkx/utils/backends.py", line 1520, in _make_doc
    return f"{self._orig_doc.rstrip()}\n\n    {to_add}"
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'rstrip'
```

### Expected Behavior

Ignore `func.__doc__` when it is None, or set `self._orig_doc` to an empty string.

Alternatively:
Just add a disclaimer to not run with -OO flag when using networkx.

### Steps to Reproduce

bug.py
```python
from networkx.utils.backends import _dispatchable
```
Run with `python -OO bug.py`

### Environment

<!--- Please provide details about your local environment -->

Python version: 3.10
NetworkX version: 3.3

### Additional context
I am not familiar with networkx. This came up when using pytorch.compile and trying out the -OO flag, which I had never heard of. I am not sure how widespread the use of the flag is or how important it is to support it. Just seems like something to be aware of. In any case, at least this edge case will now be documented for future reference.

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

* [ ] documentation for users
* [ ] documentation for backend authors
* [ ] discuss: what other information to store in the `BackendInformation` object? 
	* homepage URL
	* fancy name? (different from the name used in the entry point)
	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

## To do
* [x] change to one `can_has` function per backend. Pass in function name, it can still distribute the work if it wants to.
* [x] function naming, should it be `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error` or `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error`? The latter seems nicer, but I don't know how to do it
* [ ] documentation for users
* [ ] documentation for backend authors
* [ ] discuss: what other information to store in the `BackendInformation` object? 
	* homepage URL
	* fancy name? (different from the name used in the entry point)
	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

Summary:

This PR introduces a new **`execute_parallel`** function that simplifies algorithm parallelization logic by obviating the need for separate joblib calls for each algorithm while enabling much greater flexibility (for developers and the user).

## Key Updates:

1. **Add `execute_parallel`**:
   - Centralizes logic for parallel execution across data chunks.
   - Uses `iterator_func` to customize how data (nodes, edges, etc.) is iterated over.
   - Supports both default and custom chunking via `get_chunks`.

2. **Remove `create_iterables`**:
   - Simplified by moving to `iterator_func` within `execute_parallel`.

3. **Thread-safe Joblib config**:
   - Added a `parallel_config` context manager that uses thread-local storage to manage Joblib settings (like backend/verbose) without interference during concurrent runs.

4. **Refactor `betweenness_centrality` & `edge_betweenness_centrality`** to use `execute_parallel` as a POC.

## Why This Matters:

- **Parsimony**: Reduces code complexity by consolidating parallel execution logic into one function, making the codebase cleaner and easier to maintain.
- **Flexibility**: `execute_parallel` and `iterator_func` make this adaptable for any graph algs that need parallelism.
- **DRY**: Centralized parallel logic reduces duplication.
- **Maintainability**: Easier to extend and manage without `create_iterables`.

- ~~Perform regression test to ensure equivalent functionality~~

Summary:

This PR introduces a new **`execute_parallel`** function that simplifies algorithm parallelization logic by obviating the need for separate joblib calls for each algorithm while enabling much greater flexibility (for developers and the user).

## Key Updates:

1. **Add `execute_parallel`**:
   - Centralizes logic for parallel execution across data chunks.
   - Uses `iterator_func` to customize how data (nodes, edges, etc.) is iterated over.
   - Supports both default and custom chunking via `get_chunks`.

2. **Remove `create_iterables`**:
   - Simplified by moving to `iterator_func` within `execute_parallel`.

3. **Thread-safe Joblib config**:
   - Added a `parallel_config` context manager that uses thread-local storage to manage Joblib settings (like backend/verbose) without interference during concurrent runs.

4. **Refactor `betweenness_centrality` & `edge_betweenness_centrality`** to use `execute_parallel` as a POC.

## Why This Matters:

- **Parsimony**: Reduces code complexity by consolidating parallel execution logic into one function, making the codebase cleaner and easier to maintain.
- **Flexibility**: `execute_parallel` and `iterator_func` make this adaptable for any graph algs that need parallelism.
- **DRY**: Centralized parallel logic reduces duplication.
- **Maintainability**: Easier to extend and manage without `create_iterables`.

Description

This PR implements a backend dispatching mechanism. There is a basic backend https://github.com/betatim/scikit-image-backend-phony that you can use to experiment with the dispatching mechanism.

A backend has to provide an entry-point that points to a namespace that contains the functions which the backend implements. The namespace has to be structured like the scikit-image namespace.

In addition a backend can provide a second entry-point which provides information about the backend. For example which functions it implements. This entry-point has to work even if exotic hardware that the backend relies on is not available. For example so that the scikit-image docs building process can import the entry-point on a run of the mill CI instance.

The dispatching mechanism is similar to what is in #7513 and #7466

## To do
* [x] change to one `can_has` function per backend. Pass in function name, it can still distribute the work if it wants to.
* [x] function naming, should it be `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error` or `skimage.metrics.simple_metrics.mean_squared_error`? The latter seems nicer, but I don't know how to do it
* [ ] documentation for users
* [ ] documentation for backend authors
* [ ] discuss: what other information to store in the `BackendInformation` object? 
	* homepage URL
	* fancy name? (different from the name used in the entry point)
	* URL of a JSON file with up to date information (see "use javascript to fetch..." point above)
	* version compatibility info? Better expressed via `pyproject/toml`/dont allow the backend package to be installed together with an incompatible scikit-image version?

{"action":"created","review":{"id":2400881715,"node_id":"PRR_kwDOAA2WCc6PGowz","user":{"login":"Schefflera-Arboricola","id":91629733,"node_id":"U_kgDOBXYopQ","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/91629733?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/Schefflera-Arboricola","html_url":"https://github.com/Schefflera-Arboricola","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Schefflera-Arboricola/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Schefflera-Arboricola/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Schefflera-Arboricola/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Schefflera-Arboricola/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Schefflera-Arboricola/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Schefflera-Arboricola/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Schefflera-Arboricola/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Schefflera-Arboricola/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Schefflera-Arboricola/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"body":"Rather than adding stub functions in NetworkX to enable backend-only functions, could we instead temporarily add the stubs for backend-only functions from all the installed backends directly to NetworkX's namespace when NetworkX is imported? This way backend developers would be able to integrate backend-only functions without needing to request NetworkX to add stub functions, eliminating any bias toward specific backends.

Something like this:

In NetworkX(inside `__init__.py`):
```python
backend_only_combined = []
backends = _get_backends("networkx.backends")
for backend_name in backends:
    _backend = _load_backend(backend_name)
    if hasattr(_backend, backend_only):
        for func_name, func in _backend.backend_only.items():
             if func_name not in backend_only_combined: 
                _dispatchable(func_name, is_stub=True)
                backend_only_combined.append(func_name)
```

In backend:
```python
from nx_backend import leiden


BackendInterface.backend_only = {
    "leiden": leiden
}
```
here, `BackendInterface` is the object pointed by the `"networkx.backends"` entry_point. And `backend_only` doesn't have to be a dictionary, we can allow it to be any object, with the additional functions as its attributes.

all,

This contribution implements DomiRank centrality to networkx using scipy.sparse.csr_arrays, providing both an analytical and iterative solution (using Newton iteration). It would be great to have the addition of DomiRank as a centrality measure in networkx, as this has been requested to me a couple of times. 

DomiRank centrality is a new metric that quantifies the dominance of nodes in their neighborhoods, where, the tunable competition parameter $\sigma$ provides a trade-off between the amount of local and global topological information considered. By setting $\sigma$ very large, you are finding the most 'dominant' nodes with respect to the entire system, and by setting $\sigma \to 0$, you are converging to degree centrality - i.e. only local information.

The paper that introduces domirank is hereunder:

Engsig, M., Tejedor, A., Moreno, Y. et al. DomiRank Centrality reveals structural fragility of complex networks via node dominance. Nat Commun 15, 56 (2024). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-44257-0

I would like to apologize in advance if I am not following the contribution standards 100%, this is my first time, and if there are additional things i need to do before this can be contributed, just let me know, and I will do it as soon as possible!

Also, there are some additional things to add - e.g. finding the optimal value of $\sigma$ for largest-connected-component deterioration with node removals. I already have this in DomiRank repository, however, lets start with just the non-automated DomiRank... first things first! 

https://github.com/mengsig/DomiRank

Best,

Summary

This PR focuses on stylistic improvements and cleanup of utility functions.

### Goal
Ensure better package maintainability, scalability, and ease of contribution for developers.

### Code Style Adjustments
- Refactored variable names and formatting to improve readability.
- Improved indentation, spacing, and overall syntax compliance with PEP8.

### Utility Function Cleanup
- Introduced `@assign_algorithms` decorator to dynamically assign algorithms to `BackendInterface`, reducing manual updates and boilerplate.
- Simplified `BackendInterface` by replacing explicit algorithm declarations with automatic mapping from the `ALGORITHMS` list.
  - Even `ALGORITHMS` could be obviated by dynamically retrieving algorithm names directly from the modules using introspection (`__str__`, `dir()`, or `__dict__`), which might be too "auto-magical" for now but worth considering for a future PR.
- Improved `ParallelGraph` with type hints and clearer instantiation for better readability and consistency.
- Reduced documentation and maintenance overhead through a more scalable, dynamic approach to algorithm registration.
- Minor logic refactoring for efficiency.

Summary

This PR focuses on stylistic improvements and cleanup of utility functions.

### Goal
Ensure better package maintainability, scalability, and ease of contribution for developers.

### Code Style Adjustments
- Refactored variable names and formatting to improve readability.
- Improved indentation, spacing, and overall syntax compliance with PEP8.

### Utility Function Cleanup
- Introduced `@assign_algorithms` decorator to dynamically assign algorithms to `BackendInterface`, reducing manual updates and boilerplate.
- Simplified `BackendInterface` by replacing explicit algorithm declarations with automatic mapping from the `ALGORITHMS` list.
  - Even `ALGORITHMS` could be obviated by dynamically retrieving algorithm names directly from the modules using introspection (`__str__`, `dir()`, or `__dict__`), which might be too "auto-magical" for now but worth considering for a future PR.
- Improved `ParallelGraph` with type hints and clearer instantiation for better readability and consistency.
- Reduced documentation and maintenance overhead through a more scalable, dynamic approach to algorithm registration.
- Minor logic refactoring for efficiency.

### Removal of Unused Imports/Code
- Eliminated unused imports, reducing code complexity and improving load time.

the [Dispatching, Backend Selection, and Compatibility APIs](https://pretalx.com/euroscipy-2024/talk/8MXPRW/) discussion at EuroSciPy 2024 (for reference - https://hackmd.io/@seberg/spatch), it was proposed to separate exception handling and input validation from the core implementation of algorithms. This would result in more maintainable backend code and a better experience for backend developers, and also would reduce redundant code across backend packages. We briefly discussed this in a NetworkX dispatch meeting but never followed up.

```.py
def validator(G, ...):
    if not G: 
        raise nx.NetworkXError("Expected non-empty NetworkX graph!")
    return ...
        
@dispatchable(validator)
def nx_func(G, ...):
    ...
```

### Challenges:

- Large-scale refactoring of the main networkx repository's codebase.
- Not all exceptions could be handled in the `validator`, like `ExceededMaxIterations`, `PowerIterationFailedConvergence`, etc.(raised in the middle of algorithm's core implementation)

### Proposed Changes:

- Update the `_dispatchable` decorator to handle the `validator` function.
- Start by refactoring only the algorithms implemented in the backends. Gradually refactor other algorithms as we proceed, rather than updating everything at once. Incremental refactoring minimizes disruption to the codebase and also reduces contributing and reviewing effort.

This refactoring could be something I could conduct at the PyCon India's sprint([proposal submitted](https://in.pycon.org/cfp/devsprint-2024/proposals/networkx-and-nx-parallel-sprint~dJ6Wl/)) this month. LMK your thoughts on this and then we can accordingly put a "sprint" and/or "good-first" label on this issue.

the [Dispatching, Backend Selection, and Compatibility APIs](https://pretalx.com/euroscipy-2024/talk/8MXPRW/) discussion at EuroSciPy 2024 (for reference - https://hackmd.io/@seberg/spatch), it was proposed to separate exception handling and input validation from the core implementation of algorithms. This would result in more maintainable backend code and a better experience for backend developers, and also would reduce redundant code across backend packages. We briefly discussed this in a NetworkX dispatch meeting but never followed up.

```.py
def validator(G, ...):
    if not G: 
        raise nx.NetworkXError("Expected non-empty NetworkX graph!")
    return ...
        
@dispatchable(validator)
def nx_func(G, ...):
    ...
```

### Challenges:

- Large-scale refactoring of the main networkx repository's codebase.
- Not all exceptions could be handled in the `validator`, like `ExceededMaxIterations`, `PowerIterationFailedConvergence`, etc.(raised in the middle of algorithm's core implementation)

### Proposed Changes:

- Update the `_dispatchable` decorator to handle the `validator` function.
- Start by refactoring only the algorithms implemented in the backends. Gradually refactor other algorithms as we proceed, rather than updating everything at once. Incremental refactoring minimizes disruption to the codebase and also reduces contributing and reviewing effort.

This refactoring could be something I could conduct at the PyCon India's sprint([proposal submitted](https://in.pycon.org/cfp/devsprint-2024/proposals/networkx-and-nx-parallel-sprint~dJ6Wl/)) this month. LMK your thoughts on this and then we can accordingly put a "sprint" and/or "good-first" label on this issue.


Thank you Summary

This PR focuses on stylistic improvements and cleanup of utility functions.

### Goal
Ensure better package maintainability, scalability, and ease of contribution for new developers.

### Code Style Adjustments
- Refactored variable names and formatting to improve readability.
- Improved indentation, spacing, and overall syntax compliance with PEP8.

### Utility Function Cleanup
- Introduced `@assign_algorithms` decorator to dynamically assign algorithms to `BackendInterface`, reducing manual updates and boilerplate.
- Simplified `BackendInterface` by replacing explicit algorithm declarations with automatic mapping from the `ALGORITHMS` list.
  - Even `ALGORITHMS` could be obviated by dynamically retrieving algorithm names directly from the modules using introspection (`__str__`, `dir()`, or `__dict__`), which might be too "auto-magical" for now but worth considering for a future PR.
- Improved `ParallelGraph`'s readability and consistency.
- Reduced documentation and maintenance overhead through a more scalable, dynamic approach to algorithm registration.
- Minor logic refactoring for efficiency.

### Removal of Unused Imports/Code
- Eliminated unused imports, reducing code complexity and improving load time.

Summary

This PR focuses on stylistic improvements and cleanup of utility functions.

### Goal
Ensure better package maintainability, scalability, and ease of contribution for new developers.

### Code Style Adjustments
- Refactored variable names and formatting to improve readability.
- Improved indentation, spacing, and overall syntax compliance with PEP8.

### Utility Function Cleanup
- Introduced `@assign_algorithms` decorator to dynamically assign algorithms to `BackendInterface`, reducing manual updates and boilerplate.
- Simplified `BackendInterface` by replacing explicit algorithm declarations with automatic mapping from the `ALGORITHMS` list.
  - Even `ALGORITHMS` could be obviated by dynamically retrieving algorithm names directly from the modules using introspection (`__str__`, `dir()`, or `__dict__`), which might be too "auto-magical" for now but worth considering for a future PR.
- Improved `ParallelGraph`'s readability and consistency.
- Reduced documentation and maintenance overhead through a more scalable, dynamic approach to algorithm registration.
- Minor logic refactoring for efficiency.

### Removal of Unused Imports/Code
- Eliminated unused imports, reducing code complexity and improving load time.

Summary

This PR focuses on stylistic improvements and cleanup of utility functions.

### Goal
Ensure better package maintainability, scalability, and ease of contribution for new developers.

### Code Style Adjustments
- Refactored variable names and formatting to improve readability.
- Improved indentation, spacing, and overall syntax compliance with PEP8.

### Utility Function Cleanup
- Introduced `@assign_algorithms` decorator to dynamically assign algorithms to `BackendInterface`, reducing manual updates and boilerplate.
- Simplified `BackendInterface` by replacing explicit algorithm declarations with automatic mapping from the `ALGORITHMS` list.
  - Even `ALGORITHMS` could be obviated by dynamically retrieving algorithm names directly from the modules using introspection (`__str__`, `dir()`, or `__dict__`), which might be too "auto-magical" for now but worth considering for a future PR.
- Improved `ParallelGraph`'s readability and consistency.
- Reduced documentation and maintenance overhead through a more scalable, dynamic approach to algorithm registration.
- Minor logic refactoring for efficiency.

### Removal of Unused Imports/Code
- Eliminated unused imports, reducing code complexity and improving load time.

Summary

This PR focuses on stylistic improvements and cleanup of utility functions.

### Goal
Ensure better package maintainability, scalability, and ease of contribution for new developers.

### Code Style Adjustments
- Refactored variable names and formatting to improve readability.
- Improved indentation, spacing, and overall syntax compliance with PEP8.

### Utility Function Cleanup
- Introduced `@assign_algorithms` decorator to dynamically assign algorithms to `BackendInterface`, reducing manual updates and boilerplate.
- Simplified `BackendInterface` by replacing explicit algorithm declarations with automatic mapping from the `ALGORITHMS` list.
  - Even `ALGORITHMS` could be obviated by dynamically retrieving algorithm names directly from the modules using introspection (`__str__`, `dir()`, or `__dict__`), which might be too "auto-magical" for now but worth considering for a future PR.
- Improved `ParallelGraph`'s readability and consistency.
- Reduced documentation and maintenance overhead through a more scalable, dynamic approach to algorithm registration.
- Minor logic refactoring for efficiency.

### Removal of Unused Imports/Code
- Eliminated unused imports, reducing code complexity and improving load time.

Summary

This PR focuses on stylistic improvements and cleanup of utility functions.

### Goal
Ensure better package maintainability, scalability, and ease of contribution for new developers.

### Code Style Adjustments
- Refactored variable names and formatting to improve readability.
- Improved indentation, spacing, and overall syntax compliance with PEP8.

### Utility Function Cleanup
- Introduced `@assign_algorithms` decorator to dynamically assign algorithms to `BackendInterface`, reducing manual updates and boilerplate.
- Simplified `BackendInterface` by replacing explicit algorithm declarations with automatic mapping from the `ALGORITHMS` list.
  - Even `ALGORITHMS` could be obviated by dynamically retrieving algorithm names directly from the modules using introspection (`__str__`, `dir()`, or `__dict__`), which might be too "auto-magical" for now but worth considering for a future PR.
- Improved `ParallelGraph`'s readability and consistency.
- Reduced documentation and maintenance overhead through a more scalable, dynamic approach to algorithm registration.
- Minor logic refactoring for efficiency.

### Removal of Unused Imports/Code
- Eliminated unused imports, reducing code complexity and improving load time.

the [Dispatching, Backend Selection, and Compatibility APIs](https://pretalx.com/euroscipy-2024/talk/8MXPRW/) discussion at EuroSciPy 2024 (for reference - https://hackmd.io/@seberg/spatch), it was proposed to separate exception handling and input validation from the core implementation of algorithms. This would result in more maintainable backend code and a better experience for backend developers, and also would reduce redundant code across backend packages. We briefly discussed this in a NetworkX dispatch meeting but never followed up.

```.py
def validator(G, ...):
    if not G: 
        raise nx.NetworkXError("Expected non-empty NetworkX graph!")
    return ...
        
@dispatchable(validator)
def nx_func(G, ...):
    ...
```

### Challenges:

- Large-scale refactoring of the main networkx repository's codebase.
- Not all exceptions could be handled in the `validator`, like `ExceededMaxIterations`, `PowerIterationFailedConvergence`, etc.(raised in the middle of algorithm's core implementation)

### Proposed Changes:

- Update the `_dispatchable` decorator to handle the `validator` function.
- Start by refactoring only the algorithms implemented in the backends. Gradually refactor other algorithms as we proceed, rather than updating everything at once. Incremental refactoring minimizes disruption to the codebase and also reduces contributing and reviewing effort.

This refactoring could be something I could conduct at the PyCon India's sprint([proposal submitted](https://in.pycon.org/cfp/devsprint-2024/proposals/networkx-and-nx-parallel-sprint~dJ6Wl/)) this month. LMK your thoughts on this and then we can accordingly put a "sprint" and/or "good-first" label on this issue.

Summary

This PR focuses on stylistic improvements and cleanup of utility functions.

### Goal
Ensure better package maintainability, scalability, and ease of contribution for new developers.

### Code Style Adjustments
- Refactored variable names and formatting to improve readability.
- Improved indentation, spacing, and overall syntax compliance with PEP8.

### Utility Function Cleanup
- Introduced `@assign_algorithms` decorator to dynamically assign algorithms to `BackendInterface`, reducing manual updates and boilerplate.
- Simplified `BackendInterface` by replacing explicit algorithm declarations with automatic mapping from the `ALGORITHMS` list.
  - Even `ALGORITHMS` could be obviated by dynamically retrieving algorithm names directly from the modules using introspection (`__str__`, `dir()`, or `__dict__`), which might be too "auto-magical" for now but worth considering for a future PR.
- Improved `ParallelGraph`'s readability and consistency.
- Reduced documentation and maintenance overhead through a more scalable, dynamic approach to algorithm registration.
- Minor logic refactoring for efficiency.

### Removal of Unused Imports/Code
- Eliminated unused imports, reducing code complexity and improving load time.

Summary

This PR focuses on stylistic improvements and cleanup of utility functions.

### Goal
Ensure better package maintainability, scalability, and ease of contribution for new developers.

### Code Style Adjustments
- Refactored variable names and formatting to improve readability.
- Improved indentation, spacing, and overall syntax compliance with PEP8.

### Utility Function Cleanup
- Introduced `@assign_algorithms` decorator to dynamically assign algorithms to `BackendInterface`, reducing manual updates and boilerplate.
- Simplified `BackendInterface` by replacing explicit algorithm declarations with automatic mapping from the `ALGORITHMS` list.
  - Even `ALGORITHMS` could be obviated by dynamically retrieving algorithm names directly from the modules using introspection (`__str__`, `dir()`, or `__dict__`), which might be too "auto-magical" for now but worth considering for a future PR.
- Improved `ParallelGraph`'s readability and consistency.
- Reduced documentation and maintenance overhead through a more scalable, dynamic approach to algorithm registration.
- Minor logic refactoring for efficiency.

### Removal of Unused Imports/Code
- Eliminated unused imports, reducing code complexity and improving load time.

Summary

This PR focuses on stylistic improvements and cleanup of utility functions.

### Goal
Ensure better package maintainability, scalability, and ease of contribution for new developers.

### Code Style Adjustments
- Refactored variable names and formatting to improve readability.
- Improved indentation, spacing, and overall syntax compliance with PEP8.

### Utility Function Cleanup
- Introduced `@assign_algorithms` decorator to dynamically assign algorithms to `BackendInterface`, reducing manual updates and boilerplate.
- Simplified `BackendInterface` by replacing explicit algorithm declarations with automatic mapping from the `ALGORITHMS` list.
  - Even `ALGORITHMS` could be obviated by dynamically retrieving algorithm names directly from the modules using introspection (`__str__`, `dir()`, or `__dict__`), which might be too "auto-magical" for now but worth considering for a future PR.
- Improved `ParallelGraph`'s readability and consistency.
- Reduced documentation and maintenance overhead through a more scalable, dynamic approach to algorithm registration.
- Minor logic refactoring for efficiency.

### Removal of Unused Imports/Code
- Eliminated unused imports, reducing code complexity and improving load time.

Summary

This PR focuses on stylistic improvements and cleanup of utility functions.

### Goal
Ensure better package maintainability, scalability, and ease of contribution for new developers.

### Code Style Adjustments
- Refactored variable names and formatting to improve readability.
- Improved indentation, spacing, and overall syntax compliance with PEP8.

### Utility Function Cleanup
- Introduced `@assign_algorithms` decorator to dynamically assign algorithms to `BackendInterface`, reducing manual updates and boilerplate.
- Simplified `BackendInterface` by replacing explicit algorithm declarations with automatic mapping from the `ALGORITHMS` list.
  - Even `ALGORITHMS` could be obviated by dynamically retrieving algorithm names directly from the modules using introspection (`__str__`, `dir()`, or `__dict__`), which might be too "auto-magical" for now but worth considering for a future PR.
- Improved `ParallelGraph`'s readability and consistency.
- Reduced documentation and maintenance overhead through a more scalable, dynamic approach to algorithm registration.
- Minor logic refactoring for efficiency.

### Removal of Unused Imports/Code
- Eliminated unused imports, reducing code complexity and improving load time.

Embarrassingly parallel algorithms

Embarrassingly parallel algorithms are those that can be easily and efficiently divided into smaller, independent tasks that can be executed concurrently across multiple processing units, such as CPUs, GPUs, or nodes, without requiring significant communication or synchronisation between them. This type of parallelism is often referred to as “embarrassingly parallel” because it’s so straightforward and easy to implement. Refer [this](https://joblib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/parallel.html) to see how to implement embarrassingly parallel algorithms using joblib.

Characteristics of Embarrassingly Parallel Problems(Algorithms):

- Independent tasks: Each task can be executed independently, without relying on the output of other tasks.
- No communication: Tasks do not require frequent or significant communication with each other.
- No data dependencies: Tasks do not rely on shared data or intermediate results from other tasks.
- Easy to divide: The problem can be easily split into smaller, parallelizable tasks.

## Adding a new algorithm to nx-parallel

### Step 1 : Find a NetworkX algorithm that is embarrassingly parallel

- You can find such an algorithm from the NetworkX's references - https://networkx.org/documentation/latest/reference/index.html
- Make sure there is a `_dispatchable` decorator(in the networkx's codebase) on the algorithm you have selected to parallelise.

### Step 2 : Complete the checklist in Contributor's guide

This [checklist](https://github.com/networkx/nx-parallel/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#general-guidelines-on-adding-a-new-algorithm) in Contributor's guide for adding a new algorithm to the package.

## Some references:

It would be better to look at [currently existing algorithms](https://github.com/networkx/nx-parallel/tree/main/nx_parallel/algorithms) than previous PRs that add parallel algorithms(like https://github.com/networkx/nx-parallel/pull/60 , https://github.com/networkx/nx-parallel/pull/37 , https://github.com/networkx/nx-parallel/pull/45 and many more) because we have changed a few things. 



Feel free to ask questions if you get stuck anywhere or if anything is not clear or if you want something to be explained in a bit more detail here.
